_comment: P1-87 -- an unrecognised StopGuard.OnMissing silently disables the stop guard. Found because mutate_p184's OnMissing mutant SURVIVED against 1180 green tests. The red tests are the three TestP187_* methods in tests/RiskGuardAddOnTests.cs; they are written and RED. Tests are protected.

tickets.title: A stop action the guard cannot perform must protect the position and fail preflight
tickets.defect:
`P1-87`. `EvaluateGraceExpiry` dispatches on `_config.StopGuard.OnMissing` with two exact string comparisons and NO else branch (`addons/RiskGuardAddOn.cs`, the `== "AutoStop"` / `else if (== "Flatten")` pair). Any other value -- a lower-case `"flatten"`, a typo, an empty string, or the `"WarnOnly"` that the declaration's own comment advertises -- matches nothing, so the method emits NO ACTION AT ALL. A position with no stop, past its grace period, and the guard simply returns.

Nothing validates it. `RunPreflight` refuses an unrecognised guard MODE and has never looked at this. So the failure is silent at startup and silent at the moment it matters, while the config file still reads as though the guard is watching.

⚠️ HOW IT WAS FOUND, because it says something about the tests: a mutant in `mutation/mutate_p184.py` changed `OnMissing` from `"Flatten"` to `"AutoStop"` and the entire suite of 1180 tests stayed green. Nothing pinned the guard's most consequential default, and looking at why led here.

`"WarnOnly"` is the same defect written in a comment instead of a config file: an option offered on the declaration that produces neither an action nor a warning.
tickets.spec:
Two halves, both in `addons/RiskGuardAddOn.cs`.

A. FAIL SAFE AT DISPATCH. Give the `OnMissing` dispatch in `EvaluateGraceExpiry` an else branch that falls back to the SAME action the `"Flatten"` branch produces -- the FlattenPosition GuardAction with RuleId `MISSING_STOP_FLATTEN` and the FlattenPending state transition -- so an unrecognised action can never mean "do nothing".

Flatten is the right fallback because it is the documented default and it is the one that is always a known quantity: the alternative invents a stop at a guessed offset. Do NOT invent a new RuleId for the fallback -- the log is grepped by RuleId, and splitting one outcome across two names makes it unfindable. Restructure the dispatch so the Flatten branch and the fallback are ONE branch rather than two copies of the same action; two copies of one rule is what `P1-85`'s third slice had to undo.

B. REFUSE IT AT PREFLIGHT. Add a check to `RunPreflight` that fails when `StopGuard.OnMissing` is not one of the two values the guard actually branches on. The failure message MUST contain the offending value, because the operator's next question is what to change. Put it with the other config checks; it applies in every mode, including shadow -- a shadow-mode guard reporting actions it would have taken is exactly as wrong when the action is unreachable.

C. STOP ADVERTISING `WarnOnly`. Remove it from the `OnMissing` declaration's comment and from anywhere else in this file that offers it. It has never been implemented. Implementing it is a feature and is NOT this ticket; the string must not appear in `addons/RiskGuardAddOn.cs` at all when you are done, and a test asserts exactly that.

WHAT NOT TO DO:
* Do NOT make the comparison case-insensitive INSTEAD of the above. That silently accepts `"flatten"` and still silently accepts `"Flaten"`; it narrows the hole rather than closing it. (Doing it as well is fine, but the fallback and the preflight check are what is being asked for.)
* Do NOT change what `"AutoStop"` or `"Flatten"` do. The existing StopGuard tests cover both and must stay green.
* Do NOT add a third action.
* Do NOT touch `StopAttachSeconds` or the offsets table.
tickets.context:
THE THREE TESTS. The first drives five bad spellings -- `"flatten"`, `"FLATTEN"`, `"WarnOnly"`, `"Flaten"`, `""` -- through the real `EvaluateGraceExpiry` path with a live unstopped position, and requires a protective action for each. The second calls `RunPreflight` in SHADOW mode with exactly one connected account and FirmMirror off, so every other preflight check passes and the new one is the only thing that can fail -- `PreflightResult.Fail` OVERWRITES, so a second failure would hide the first. It also asserts a RECOGNISED action still passes, which is the control. The third is a source scan for `WarnOnly`.

ASCII only. C# 8.0 / .NET Framework 4.8 and a net8.0 test build. The lock-scope rule applies: `EvaluateGraceExpiry` collects intent and must not call into `Account`.
expect_green: still produces a protective action rather than silence
an action the guard does not implement fails preflight
and the message names the value it could not perform
nothing in the guard mentions WarnOnly

regions.anchor: internal List<GuardAction> EvaluateGraceExpiry(Account account, string instrument)
regions.note: THE WHOLE METHOD, because the OnMissing dispatch is an if/else-if chain and a region that covers only the `if` leaves a dangling `else` -- four rounds of the previous run failed to compile on exactly that. AutoStop keeps its branch; Flatten and the unrecognised case become ONE branch producing one action with one RuleId. Everything else in this method -- the coverage arithmetic, the FSM state checks, the early returns -- stays as it is.
THE VALIDATION. One more check beside the existing mode check. Every other check in this method stays exactly as it is.
THE DECLARATION COMMENT that advertises WarnOnly. Delete the advertisement only -- StopAttachSeconds and its P1-84 comment, MaxAutoStopAttempts and the offsets table all stay.
